old: Read this slowly into a recorder, speak it aloud, or learn its movement and use silent words if that comes easily. Choose one anchor—a sound, bodily contact, or your two-hand practice—and an opening phrase. Keep using the same anchor where the words refer to it. Pause between paragraphs; don’t read the delivery directions aloud.
Let your eyes settle somewhere in the room, somewhere they can rest for a little while, and notice the difference between looking for something and letting what is already there come into view.

There is a surface beneath you. Notice where you meet it … the contact, the pressure, whatever you can actually feel. And while you notice that, a sound may reach you, or a breath may draw your attention, without needing you to arrange either one.
You can give this a little time.

A thought about the day may still be here. A thought about whether you’re doing this properly may be here too. There is room to notice a thought and return to the anchor you chose, without finishing the thought first.

And as you return, you may find one detail that holds your interest … something about the sound, or the contact, or that particular way of listening … and let attention stay with it long enough to become curious.

Perhaps you can give yourself the time you would give someone you care about who has begun to speak and hasn’t yet found the words. You can remain nearby, listening, without finishing their sentence for them.
Let your chosen phrase come to mind now. Say it as an invitation, and notice how it is received.
As you continue, your eyes can close, soften, or stay open. Let that be a choice you make. Listening may deepen while a sound from the room remains available in the background.
Count slowly from five to one. Give each number its own moment.

Five. Notice your chosen anchor again. Four. Let attention gather around what you find. Three. Leave a little space after the words. Two. Listen into that space, without preparing an answer. One. Stay here for a moment.
Bring your chosen concern lightly to mind, or remain with your wish for contact. Let it be present without rehearsing its whole story.
What am I noticing now?
Give the response time to take its own form. It might be a sensation, a few words, an image, a feeling, or an impulse to move. There may be nothing clear yet.
Leave room to notice, with words or without them.
new: Practise reading the following slowly into the recorder or read it aloud or learn it and say it silently. Decide whether to use sound, bodily contact or the two hands as your anchor throughout. Choose one of the opening phrases to use in the following. Whenever you see ‘the anchor’ in the following say the anchor you’ve chosen. Pause at the end of each paragraph for a few moments. Don’t read aloud the instructions for how to do the reading.
Begin by allowing your eyes to settle somewhere in the room
Notice the contact between your body and the surface that you are on. Notice the feel of that contact. As you notice the contact notice too the sound / your breath
There’s time to do this

Perhaps there are some thoughts, about things that have happened today, or perhaps about doing this thing properly, whatever it is, can you turn your attention back to the anchor even if there is a thought there
Perhaps there is something in the way that you are listening to the sound, or touching your body, or holding your hands that catches your attention.
Give yourself the time you would give to someone you were really interested in hearing, who has started to talk to you, but is not yet saying what he or she wanted to.
Notice what comes to you when you say the phrase: <your chosen phrase here>
You can close your eyes, soften them or keep them open as you proceed, it’s up to you. As you listen your listening may deepen but you may always return to the sound in the room.
Count slowly to yourself from 5 to 1
As you say 5 notice again your chosen anchor. 4 3 2 1 Take a moment here
Bring to mind gently the thing you’ve chosen to work with today / your wish to make contact
What do you notice now?
Take some time to notice whatever comes, it might be sensations, it might be words, it might be images, it might be feelings, it might be urges to move your body in some way, it might be nothing.
Take some time to notice this, with or without words

old: Use this when loveyhuasca, meditation, lucid dreaming, grief, music, prayer, erotic energy, exhaustion, or intense beauty has already opened the state. Stabilize before making it stronger.
“The state is already open. I do not need to intensify it. I need to aim it, stabilize it, and keep it kind.”

Look around the room. Name where you are. Name the date, or at least the day. Feel your feet, hands, and spine. Press your thumbs gently but firmly against your index fingers. Focus on the physical friction of skin meeting skin.
“Only what can be integrated is welcome now. Anything too much can wait. The body may stay safe. The adult self remains present. The inner child does not have to carry this alone.”
Once you’re oriented, choose one intention:
“Please show me the next useful truth, symbol, feeling, question, or action — only in the amount I can live well with.”
new: This is good to use when you have opened a state through some other means, e.g. loyeuhasca, meditation, lucid dreaming, dealing with a grief, listening to music, prayer, working with erotic energy, being exhausted, being moved by something beautiful. It is to stabilise the state before you try to make it stronger.
I don’t need to intensify this state, it’s already open, I need to aim it, stabilise it and keep it kind

Look around you, notice where you are, say to yourself where you are, say to yourself the date or the day, notice your body, your feet, hands, spine. Pick one place, for instance, where your thumb meets your index finger, press them firmly together and concentrate only on the physical sensation of the friction
"I'm going to allow myself to go only as far as I am able to integrate. Too much can wait. My body is safe. I'm present as an adult. My inner child doesn't have to do this alone".
Once you're oriented, pick one of these phrases to be your intention: "Please show me the next thing I need to know, as a symbol, feeling, question or action, in a way that I can live my life."

old: Sit upright. Open the eyes. Feel the feet. Let the breath be natural.
Say: “I am not going away. I am coming more fully here.”
Look at one object. Feel the spine.
“Is this daydream guidance, emotional digestion, or avoidance?”
“If it is guidance, show me the action inside it. If it is avoidance, bring me gently into the present and show me what I am avoiding.”

If stillness makes you sleepy, diffuse, or escape-prone, hypnosis can become more alert rather than more relaxed. Keep the eyes open and pair a small repeated hand movement with increasing clarity; stop the movement and notice what remains without trying to disappear inward.

“Eyes open. Press thumb and forefinger together gently. Release. Again — clearer, not sleepier. One more time. Now stop the deliberate movement. Notice the first second after the rhythm ends. Is there an echo in the fingers, the breath, the attention, or nowhere at all? Stay upright and work from exactly that level of alertness.”
new: Sit up, open your eyes, feel your feet and breath naturally.
Acknowledge: "I'm not going to go away, I'm going to come more into myself".
Pick an object to look at and feel your spine.
Ask yourself, are you daydreaming in order to hear guidance or in order to integrate emotional experience or are you escaping from something?
If you're trying to hear guidance, ask to have the guidance to be about what to do. If you're escaping from something, ask to be brought gently into the present and shown what you're avoiding.

If you find that doing still work you escape into sleepiness or diffuse states of mind, change the work so that it is increasing levels of alertness and not relaxation. A good way to work in a state of alertness, with your eyes open, is to have the client do something with their hands for a little while and then deliberately stop doing it. For example:

"Open your eyes and press your thumb and forefinger together. Let it go. Do that a few times. Each time you let go, become more clear, more alert. Now deliberately stop doing that. Pay attention to the first second after you stop doing that. Do you feel an echo in your fingers? In your breath? In your attention? Or does it go nowhere?" Stay upright and work with that level of alertness.

old: Place one hand on the heart. Place the other hand on the solar plexus.
Let the heart hand represent the Nurturer. Let the solar plexus hand represent the vulnerable child.
Breathe gently.
“Love above. Child below. Adult present.”
“I send love to the child. I receive the child’s signal. I send love again. I listen again.”
new: Where are YOUR hands? Put one of YOUR hands on YOUR heart. Put the other of YOUR hands on YOUR solar plexis.
The hand on YOUR heart is the Nurturer. The hand on YOUR solar plexis is the vulnerable child in YOU.
Breathe gently and affirm
The love is above and the child is below. And the adult is present.
I send love down to the child. And I receive signal from the child. Then I send more love down. And I listen to the signal again.

old: Sleep induction has a different job. In inner work, the adult returns, writes, and acts. At bedtime, analysis can remain off duty. Revelation can wait; the task is rest.
For sleep hypnosis, see Nimja’s sleep playlist.
new: This induction is different from the others, because in the others you need to get all the way back to your Adult to be able to write, do things, etc. In this case, the point is to go to sleep, so it is good for analysis to NOT be on duty and for revelation to wait.
To hear a hypnosis that will put you to sleep, check out Nimja's playlist here .

old: Fractionation means returning toward ordinary awareness and then deciding whether to enter absorption again. Used openly, it teaches that trance has a door in both directions. Name the technique before using it; every answer cannot secretly mean “deeper.”

“Open the eyes and return toward ordinary awareness. Feel the room and decide whether to stop here. If you choose to continue, close or soften the eyes and notice what changes as attention gathers again. You may stop at either point.”
new: Ok, now I'd like you to open your eyes and come back. Do you want to stop the hypnosis? If not, close or soften your eyes and notice what's different as you go back into absorption. You can stop either way.

old: You can practice the core method without learning one term of Neuro-Linguistic Programming. Read this appendix when you want more precision about imagery, bodily states, rehearsal, and sentence design. NLP is useful when it helps the system listen; it becomes a bag of tricks when technique replaces love, truth, contact, or consent.
new: Appendix B - NLP (Neuro-Linguistic Programming)

You do not need to know this stuff to do it but if you want to freshen up on your skills in the art of working with imagery, body states, behavioural rehearsal, talking to yourself in effective sentences etc then it might be useful. Using the techniques can be an easy way to fall into the trap of thinking that NLP is a bag of tricks rather than something that needs to be done with love and truth and contact and consent.

old: Sensory NLP changes the form of an inner experience: image, sound, distance, size, brightness, volume, posture, pressure.
State NLP makes useful states easier to access: warmth, adult presence, courage, steadiness, love, clarity.
Strategy NLP rehearses a better response: when this cue appears, the adult does this.

Language NLP shapes the sentence: pace what is already true, open awareness, presume only safe capacity, link cause and effect carefully, embed invitations, and use de-hypnotic questions when language becomes vague, absolute, manipulative, or grandiose.
new: The four levels of NLP are:
Sensory Level of NLP: working with the form of an inner experience (where do you see or hear it, how far away, how big, how bright, how loud, how do you hold your body, where is the pressure etc.)
Strategy level of NLP: practising a better response.

Language Level of NLP: pacing what is true; opening up people’s awareness; presuming you can do something safe; linking cause and effect; embedding invitations; asking de-hypnotic questions to break the effects of vague, absolutes, manipulative or grandiose language.

old: The Milton Model concerns the architecture of the sentence. Commands such as “Relax now,” “Stop being anxious,” or “Trust me” often make a part brace.
Part of the point of indirect language is to get past that reflexive skeptical argument without having to overpower it. The destination can still be deliberate even when the route is subtle.
Begin with what is already true, lower the pressure, presume only a small safe capacity, and invite one movement:
“As the body notices the bed beneath it, it may become a little easier to stop holding the whole day alone.”
Pace reality. Open awareness. Validate function. Presuppose capacity. Bridge gently. Invite one small movement. Test with the body.
new: The Milton Model (how to talk to yourself without it being like a covert sales seminar)
What’s the problem? When you say “ Relax now” or “Stop being anxious” or “Trust me” there is often a part of me that wants to argue with you.
How do you get past the part that wants to argue with you without overpowering it so you can get to the place you want to get to?

You start with something you know to be true, you take the pressure off, you presume only a small safe capacity and you invite just one movement. E.g. “ As the body notices the bed beneath it it may become a little easier to stop holding the whole day alone.”

Notice that the sentence: Paces what is already true; Opens up awareness; Validates the function of what you want to change; Presupposes (or takes for granted) a capacity for change; Bridges the two ideas together; Invites only one movement; Tests whether it has happened or not.

old: Pacing and leading means stating what is already true before inviting anything new.
“Anxiety is here. The body is activated. A protector is trying to help. And one breath at a time, the adult can start to listen.”
The simplest form is a Truth + Invite loop:

“It is completely true that [current sensation or emotion] is here. It makes sense that my system is reacting by [current protective behavior or thought]. And right alongside that truth, my adult self is here, breathing in this room, ready to listen to whatever comes up next.”
new: It follows the pattern of pacing and leading.

An example pacing and leading with anxiety: “ It is completely true that the sensation of anxiety is here right now. It is completely true that the body has activated to meet this anxiety. It is completely true that there is a protector that wants to do this for you. It is completely true that the adult part of you can start to listen, one breath at a time.”
So the pattern is Truth, Invite, Truth, Invite etc.

An example script: “ It is completely true that the sensation of _______ (or the emotion of _____) is coming up for me right now. It makes complete sense that my system is reacting by doing/thinking ________. While that is completely true, there is also another completely true thing that my adult self is here, breathing in this room right now, and willing to listen to what comes up next.

old: Awareness verbs point attention without yelling at it: notice, realize, recognize, sense, feel, wonder, imagine, picture, listen, allow, discover, remember, consider.
“Notice whether the answer comes as an image, a word, a pressure, a warmth, a silence, or a next action.”
new: Awareness’ verbs: notice, realize, recognize, sense, feel, wonder, imagine, picture, listen, allow, discover, remember, consider . E.g. “ Notice what your body notices…”

old: A presupposition hides an assumption inside a sentence. Use that power only to presume choice, timing, capacity, safety, love, and adult leadership. Don’t smuggle in obedience.
“Before any part has to change, it can first become more understood.”
new: Presuppositions - Be very careful how you use presuppositions. They should only ever be used to presume that you have chosen, or that you will choose, or that you will have chosen to do something. Or to presume that you will, can, are able to do something safe like get in touch with a part, or be in your adult self. Or to presume that there is love, or that the adult can be in charge etc. Never use it for anything else. E.g. “ Before you change you will have understood why you were doing it in the first place”

old: Words such as as, while, because, when, after, before, and which means connect one event to another. Use them carefully. A gentle voice doesn’t make a false causal claim true.
Too strong: “Because I breathe, the trauma leaves.” Better: “As I breathe, the adult self may become present enough to hear one small piece of what the wound needs.”
new: Be careful how you link things together. Words like ‘as’, ‘while’, ‘because’, ‘when’, ‘after’, ‘before’, ‘which means’ etc are all words that are used to link events together. So e.g.
The first one is generally not good enough because it is too strong. It is unlikely that just by breathing you will get rid of a trauma. The second one is better because it is more accurate.

old: When the presence feels hostile, cold, alien, parasitic, or boundary-violating, don’t offer soft sentimental love as though inviting it in for tea. Use love with a boundary.

Sit upright. Press your feet into the floor. Let the spine rise. Gently draw the shoulder blades back so the chest is open but not exposed. Feel the skin boundary of the torso. Feel that this body has a perimeter.

“I recognize that suffering may be here, and I wish all suffering to return to the space where it belongs. But the boundary of this skin belongs to my adult life. You do not have permission to enter this house.”
“Compassion is present. The door is closed.”
new: Second, feel free to tell the presence that while you have compassion for it, the door is closed.

This is especially a good idea if the presence you’re experiencing seems even the slightest bit hostile, cold, alien, parasitic, etc. It needs to realize that you don’t welcome it and that it needs to respect your boundaries. It’s not really helpful to approach it with the kind of soft, sentimental love that you’d use if you were inviting it to stay for tea, but it can be useful to approach it with love while also making it clear that it needs to respect your boundaries.

Sit up, make sure your feet are grounded on the floor, straighten your spine, pull your shoulder blades back a little, open your chest a little, feel the boundary of your torso’s skin, feel the perimeter of your body, and tell the presence, “While I have compassion for you and any suffering you may be experiencing, this suffering needs to go back where it came from. The boundary of my skin is the boundary of an adult now, and you’re not welcome to come inside the house anymore.”
